sources.note: Phonology section gives 13 consonants, 5 vowels, phonotactics; the only stress-related remark: 'Central vowel [ə] is very common in Walker's vocabularies. It appears to be a destressed allophone of low central /a/.' No statement of where stress falls.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy & Edgar Suter. 2020. The Asmat-Muli languages of Southwestern New Guinea. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 38: 148-175.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. pp.152-153 review every Kamrau Bay source: all are lexical only; 'A tentative statement of the phoneme inventory and the personal pronouns of North and South Kamrau is presented in Voorhoeve (1975b:370). Apart from this, nothing is known about the grammar of any of the three Kamrau Bay languages.'

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 345-460. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 2.6.2.2.6.1.1 'Iria and Asienara' (pp.369-370): phoneme inventory 'as far as it could be ascertained from the wordlists' and pronouns; 'Further grammatical information is at present not available.' No mention of stress for Iria/Asienara (stress is mentioned only for Kamoro, where Drabbe marks it on words but gives no rules).

sources.note: Historical-phonology tables reproduce Walker (& Hesse 1988) pre-phonemic survey forms for S. Kamrau (Yarona) with stress marks on individual words; no rule stated. My script tally of that column (audit observation, not a published claim): 96 stress-marked polysyllabic forms, 90 marked on the first syllable, 6 on the second.
